newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: First Kazakh bank assigned international rating.
newsitem.headline: First Kazakh bank assigned international rating.

text.p: AO Kazkommertsbank said on Wednesday it had been assigned a rating of B-, the first bank to be granted a rating in the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.

"We were informed on Tuesday by the U.S. rating agency Thomson BankWatch that it had granted us a long-term hard currency borrower rating," Oleg Kononenko, head of the bank's foreign relations department, told Reuters.
"We are the first Kazakh bank to be assigned such a rating," he said.
Last year, Kazakhstan was granted a BB- rating for long-term currency bonds by rating agencies IBCA and Standard and Poor's prior to its debut Eurobond issue.
In December foreign investors snapped up the $200-million issue, double the placement originally planned.

"Our bank has received practically the same rating as Kazakhstan and this is likely to boost its image of being stable and creditworthy," Kononenko said. "This is likely to have a positive impact on relations with our foreign partners."
These partners, some of whom had earlier granted Kazkommertsbank short-term loans, include Germany's Commerzbank AG, Dutch bank ABN AMRO, U.S. Citibank and France's Societe Generale, he said.
